doc.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The In a Jazz Orbit big-band album
summary: After Red Clyde backed out he found a label; the all-star personnel played three days in the studio, and the title came from the office.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You mentioned – and I actually had this on the list – your joint group of, I guess, Bobby Brookmeyer? Is that right? In a Jazz Orbit? Or did I have the wrong credit here?

Okay. Hang on. It was February of ‟58. So let‟s see who you were paired with on that one, because it was a double credit. I‟m sorry. I can‟t read my own shorthand: Bill Holman big band, In a Jazz Orbit. This was February 11th in Los Angeles.

This was another project that Red Clyde had commissioned and then backed out at the last minute. So I was looking for somebody to record it. I did some charts for an Art Pepper date. I‟m surprised it‟s not there.
We talked about the Art Pepper Nine. No? Another Art Pepper date?

Yeah. It wasn‟t that personnel that you had. It was something to do – Latin. I can‟t remember what the name of the title was. Anyway, I did a couple of charts. I met these people and decided that I would try to push the big band record with them, and it worked. Talk about all-star personnel. We were talking about one of the things yesterday, the all-star personnel. The personnel I had on that record is astounding. I had Conte, Jack Sheldon, Rosolino, Carl Fontana.
Ray Sims on trombone, Herb Geller, Charlie Mariano, Richie, Charlie Kennedy, Bill Hood baritone, Victor Feldman, Buddy Clark, Mel Lewis.
Yeah. Talk about an all-star band. That was fun too. I mentioned that that movie date with Mandel was a lot of fun. This was fun too, just to hear those guys play.
You had three consecutive days in the studio. So that‟s great to have three days, back-to-back, to work on the material. Where did the title come from, In a Jazz Orbit?
Does it tie into the space race here?
I‟ve got used to it now, but at first it really hit me as something that shouldn‟t be there.
